headline: Classes Suspended in Parts of Metro Manila and Cavite on August 8
kicker: Weather and public safety · Metro Manila and Cavite
deck: Local authorities suspended classes in several Metro Manila cities and Cavite for Saturday, August 8, amid inclement weather linked to the southwest monsoon and tropical cyclones.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Classes were suspended in several parts of Metro Manila and in Cavite on Saturday, August 8, 2026, because of inclement weather associated with the southwest monsoon and tropical cyclones Maymay and Dolphin.

sections.heading: Areas covered
paragraphs: Caloocan, Malabon, and Manila suspended face-to-face classes at all levels in public and private schools.
Cavite, Las Piñas, Marikina, and Parañaque announced class suspensions covering all levels in public and private schools.

sections.heading: Background
paragraphs: The advisories cited inclement weather associated with the southwest monsoon and tropical cyclones Maymay and Dolphin. Class-suspension coverage differed by locality and learning arrangement because each local authority issued its own order.

sections.heading: Court operations
paragraphs: No broad weather-related suspension of court operations across Metro Manila and Southern Luzon was confirmed in the cited Supreme Court advisory. The advisory listed limited suspensions in Angeles City because of termite control and in Balayan, Tuy, and Calatagan, Batangas, because of a scheduled power interruption.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: Suspension details differ by locality and by learning arrangement. Families, students, and school personnel should check the exact wording issued by their local government and school instead of assuming that one advisory applies across the entire region.

sections.heading: What remains unclear
paragraphs: The suspension list may change as local governments issue additional advisories. Schools may also announce their own arrangements for activities not covered by a local order.

sections.heading: What happens next
paragraphs: Residents should monitor official local government, school, and PAGASA channels for updates on rainfall, flooding, transport conditions, and any changes to class arrangements.
